Merge pull request #72 from 3o14/docs/vercel-analytics

feat(docs): add Vercel Web Analytics and tag README links

Picked up by the docs prebuild step from CHANGELOG.md.

docs(readme): tag the docs links with utm_source=readme

The README is what npm and GitHub show, so tagging its links to the docs
site lets Web Analytics count visitors who arrive from it. npm and GitHub
render the same file, so both report as "readme". llms.txt is left alone
since analytics never runs on a plain text file.

sync-readme copies the README into the Storybook introduction, so it
rewrites the tag to utm_source=storybook there.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

feat(docs): add Vercel Web Analytics

Render <Analytics /> from @vercel/analytics/next in the root layout so the
docs site reports page views, referrers, and UTM parameters. Web Analytics
is enabled on the Vercel project; the script is served from
/_vercel/insights on the deployment. It uses no cookies, so no consent
banner is needed.

Verified pnpm run docs:build: the static export succeeds (25 pages) and
references /_vercel/insights.

Rejected: GA4 | cookie consent banner and a heavier script for metrics we don't need yet
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

Merge pull request #70 from 3o14/fix/dropdown-popup-theme

fix: keep the theme and primary colors on portaled popups

refactor(Dropdown): resolve the theme once through usePortalThemeProps

From review: the trigger wrapper looked up the theme class with its own lightTheme fallback next to usePortalThemeProps(), which does the same. Use portalThemeProps.className for both so they can't drift.

refactor(ThemeProvider): drop the container style memo

From review: consumers usually pass `style` inline, so a memo keyed on it
recomputed on every render anyway. Spread it directly. Also narrow the
matchMedia guard's comment to what it covers (no matchMedia at all); the
addEventListener call is unchanged from main.

docs(tokens): show the primary token fallbacks in design-tokens.json

The six primary entries said the tokens resolve only through CSS custom
properties, "not a static value". The themes now emit
var(--pie-primary-*, <default>), so list the default scale for each mode
and say where it applies.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(Tooltip): theme the portal element so design styles match

Same as Dialog: the theme class was on the popup itself, so the game pixel
box and crayon font selectors (`.${themeClass} &`) were skipped with
applyGlobal={false}. Use usePortalThemeProps() on BaseTooltip.Portal.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(Dialog): theme the portal element so design styles match

The theme class was on the popup itself, but the game and crayon container
styles in Dialog.css.ts use `.${themeClass} &`, which needs an ancestor.
With applyGlobal={false} (no class on <html>) they were skipped and a
crayon dialog rendered with the basic container. Use usePortalThemeProps()
on BaseDialog.Portal instead.

Measured in headless Chrome with design="crayon" applyGlobal={false}: the
dialog background was the basic surface on main and is now the crayon
container's transparent background.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(Dropdown): theme the portal element instead of the positioner

Use usePortalThemeProps() on BaseSelect.Portal, an ancestor of the positioner and popup, instead of setting the theme class and primary vars on the Positioner by hand.

fix(ThemeProvider): stop writing the primary vars to <html>

From review: setting --pie-primary-* on <html> with applyGlobal overrode a
consumer's own :root values and applyPrimaryColorVars(), its cleanup
deleted them, and nested providers removed each other's values on unmount.
The library's popups now get the vars on their portal element in every
mode, and the theme tokens fall back to the default scale elsewhere, so
the global write is no longer needed. Content a consumer portals outside
the provider gets the default scale rather than a custom primaryColor.

Also memoize the container style so a parent re-render doesn't rebuild it.

Rejected: Keep the <html> write and reference-count providers | more state for an edge case the fallback already covers
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

feat(ThemeProvider): add usePortalThemeProps for portaled popups

From review: Dropdown, Dialog, and Tooltip each re-applied the theme class
and primary vars by hand, on different elements, and Dialog and Tooltip put
the class on the popup itself, where `.${themeClass} &` selectors can't
match it.

usePortalThemeProps() returns { className, style } for a Base UI *.Portal
element. The portal is an ancestor of the backdrop, positioner, and popup,
so every part of the popup resolves the provider's tokens and the
design-specific selectors match. It is internal (not exported from the
package entry).

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(ThemeProvider): set the primary vars on <html> with applyGlobal

From review:
- With applyGlobal, set the computed --pie-primary-* vars on <html> next to
  the theme class, and remove them on cleanup, so content a consumer
  portals outside the provider gets a custom primaryColor too, not only the
  library's own popups.
- Restore the old precedence: the computed vars win over the same vars in
  the style prop, as they did when an effect set them on the container.
- Warn about an invalid primaryColor from an effect instead of during
  render (useMemo), so it doesn't fire during SSR or twice in StrictMode.

Measured in headless Chrome: a primary Button rendered with createPortal
under <ThemeProvider primaryColor="#e11d48"> now gets the custom color.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: Brief first-paint default color in consumer-portaled content before the effect runs (same timing as the theme class on <html>)

refactor(tokens): derive the primary var helpers from the var names

From review: getPrimaryColorVars() and primaryColorVarRefs() each spelled
out the six primary states by hand, so a new state would have to be added
in three places. Both now map over PRIMARY_COLOR_STATES, derived from
PRIMARY_COLOR_CSS_VAR_NAMES.

getPrimaryColorVars() also returns Record<string, string> again instead of
React's CSSProperties. The token utils are part of the React-free
pine-design-system/tokens graph (see src/tokens/public.ts), and the type
import ended up in the emitted declarations. Verified dist/tokens has no
react import after the build.

constants.ts's Korean doc comment is migrated to English.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

test(Tooltip): drop the matchMedia stub from the theming tests

ThemeProvider now works without window.matchMedia, so the stub isn't needed.

test(Dialog): drop the matchMedia stub from the theming tests

ThemeProvider now works without window.matchMedia, so the stub isn't needed.

test(Dropdown): drop the matchMedia stub from the theming tests

ThemeProvider now works without window.matchMedia, so the stub isn't needed.

fix(ThemeProvider): resolve the system theme without matchMedia

subscribeToSystemTheme and getSystemThemeSnapshot called
window.matchMedia unconditionally, so ThemeProvider threw wherever it is
missing (jsdom, some embedded webviews), even with syncWithSystem={false}.
Treat a missing matchMedia as light.

Also, from review: make primaryColorStyle optional on the exported
ThemeContextValue type so a hand-built value still type-checks after a
patch upgrade, and type getPrimaryColorVars() as CSSProperties so the memo
needs no casts.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(tokens): fall back to the default primary scale in every theme

The themes assigned the primary tokens as var(--pie-primary-*) with no
fallback. Only ThemeProvider sets those properties, on its container, so
anything outside it had no primary colors: components used without a
provider, and content a consumer portals outside it.

primaryColorVarRefs() builds the references with the default light or dark
primary scale as the fallback, which is the same scale ThemeProvider
applies when no primaryColor is set. All six theme modes use it.

Measured in headless Chrome with a packed build and no ThemeProvider: the
Dropdown's selected primary option and a Dialog's primary Button were
transparent on main and now use the default primary color.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(Tooltip): apply the primary color vars to the portaled popup

Same as Dialog: the popup renders in <body>, outside the provider, so apply
primaryColorStyle from the theme context on it.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(Dialog): apply the primary color vars to the portaled popup

The popup is portaled to <body>, outside the provider, so the primary
color vars that its action buttons read were unset and a primary Button
rendered with a transparent background. Apply primaryColorStyle from the
theme context on the popup.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(Dropdown): match Base UI's empty data-selected attribute

The selected-option styles targeted [data-selected='true'], but Base UI
sets data-selected with an empty value, so the selected option was never
highlighted. Target [data-selected] instead.

Measured in headless Chrome: the selected primary option's background was
transparent on main and is now the primary surface color.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(Dropdown): apply the primary color vars to the portaled popup

The popup now gets primaryColorStyle from the theme context on the
Positioner, next to the theme class, so the primary hover, focus ring, and
selected colors resolve. Also explain why the applyGlobal={false} test
asserts that <html> has no theme class: without that precondition the
closest() check would match <html> and pass without the fix.

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow

fix(ThemeProvider): expose the primary color vars for portaled popups

The themes read the primary scale from --pie-primary-* custom properties
with no fallback. ThemeProvider only set them on its container through an
effect, so popups portaled to <body> (Dropdown, Dialog, Tooltip) had no
primary colors at all: a primary Button in a Dialog rendered with a
transparent background, and primaryColor never reached any popup.

Compute the vars once with useMemo, render them on the container's style,
and expose them as primaryColorStyle on the theme context so portaled
components can apply them next to themeClass. getPrimaryColorVars() maps a
color scale to the var object; applyPrimaryColorVars() now uses it. The
file's Korean comments are migrated to English.

Measured in headless Chrome with a packed build: --pie-primary-surface was
empty in every popup on main and now matches the provider in all three
modes (global, applyGlobal={false}, custom primaryColor).

Rejected: Default --pie-primary-* inside each theme class | popups would still lose a custom primaryColor
Rejected: Portal popups into the provider container | ancestors with overflow/transform would clip them
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: moderate
Not-tested: SSR markup diff from moving the vars from an effect to the style prop

fix(Dropdown): apply the theme class to the portaled popup

The popup is portaled to <body>, outside the trigger's themed wrapper.
Dialog and Tooltip put the theme class on their portaled content, but
Dropdown didn't, so its popup only picked up theme variables when they
happened to be on <html>. With applyGlobal={false} or outside a
ThemeProvider the background and colors fell back to unset variables, and
inside a nested ThemeProvider the popup used the outer theme.

Put the theme class on the Positioner. It is an ancestor of the Popup, so
the `.${themeClass} &` selectors in Dropdown.css.ts keep matching; putting
it on the Popup itself would not.

Closes #31

Rejected: Theme class on BaseSelect.Popup (as Tooltip does) | Dropdown.css.ts targets the popup with `.${theme} &`, which needs an ancestor
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: Visual check in a browser

fix(tokens): Fix game/crayon font 404s in consumer apps

fix(storybook): point theme font URLs at /font/ in Storybook

The theme @font-face rules now use ./font/..., which matches the shipped
dist/ layout. Storybook compiles the CSS from source, so build-storybook
emitted it as assets/ThemeProvider-[hash].css and ./font/ resolved to
/assets/font/, which does not exist. The deployed Storybook would have
fallen back to a default font for the game and crayon stories. Dev only
worked by accident: Vite injects the CSS as a <style> tag, so the relative
URL resolved against /iframe.html.

Add a Storybook-only Vite plugin that rewrites url(./font/...) to
url(/font/...) in vanilla-extract CSS, where Storybook serves public/font.

Verified build-storybook output requests /font/*.woff2 (200 font/woff2) and
the dev server serves both fonts at the rewritten URLs.

Rejected: staticDirs mapping public/font to /assets/font | fixes the build only; dev keeps relying on document-relative resolution
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: Visual check of the game/crayon stories in a browser

fix(ThemeProvider): load theme stylesheets through the consumer's bundler

ThemeProvider injected a <link> to a URL built from import.meta.url. Consumer
bundlers copy that file as an opaque asset without processing its url()s, so
./font/... resolved to /assets/font/... and the game/crayon fonts still 404'd
on the documented design-switch path. In Vite dev the pre-bundled dep pointed
import.meta.url at node_modules/.vite/deps, so the stylesheet itself 404'd.

Use import() with static string specifiers instead, so the bundler processes
the CSS like any other import and emits the packaged fonts. The specifiers
were already externalized in vite.config.ts and aliased in vitest; Storybook
gets the same empty-file alias. verify-build-output now checks the dist
entries keep the static import() and do not use import.meta.url.

Verified with ThemeProvider only (no direct theme CSS import) in Vite 6 dev
and build, and Next.js 16.4 (Turbopack) dev and build: fonts load as
font/woff2 in all four.

Constraint: Specifiers must be string literals; Rollup breaks template literals here
Rejected: Keep <link> and rewrite url() in split-css | output path depends on each consumer bundler
Rejected: Variable specifier with @vite-ignore (e5454a42) | browser cannot resolve bare specifiers
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: moderate
Directive: Do not reintroduce @vite-ignore or a computed specifier; bundlers must see the literal
Not-tested: webpack-only consumers, CRA/Jest environments without CSS module handling

chore: write the font path comments, messages, and test name in English

Matches the English-only convention used elsewhere in the repo. The
"온글잎-승훈체" font-family name stays as is because it is an identifier
consumers rely on.

feat(tokens): add per-component radius tokens and stepped pixel frame helpers

A radius at or above half an element's height renders as a pill, so one
radius scale shared by components of different heights made rounded steps
collapse. Button, Badge, and inputs now get their own small/medium/large

The game theme draws its frame with box-shadow, which border-radius can't
round. gamePixel.css.ts builds the frame from a trim var (negative spread
shortens each side) and paints inner corner cells with background-image,
giving square / notched / two-step corners. shadow.pixelColor exposes the
frame color on its own so solid variants can build that frame.

Merge pull request #64 from 3o14/ci/npm-trusted-publishing

fix(ci): publish to npm with trusted publishing instead of NPM_TOKEN

fix(ci): drop registry-url and pin npm in the release workflow

- registry-url makes setup-node write a placeholder NODE_AUTH_TOKEN into
  .npmrc. If the OIDC exchange fails, npm falls back to it and the registry
  answers with the same misleading 404 this branch fixes. Without it, a
  missing trusted publisher surfaces as a plain auth error
- Pin npm to 11.21.0 instead of ^11.5.1, so a job holding id-token: write
  doesn't run whatever 11.x is newest that day
- Note that the npm upgrade matters because pnpm 9 delegates publish to npm

Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: actual OIDC publish (needs the npmjs.com trusted publisher setting first)

fix(ci): publish to npm with trusted publishing instead of NPM_TOKEN

The 1.2.0 release failed with "404 Not Found - PUT .../pine-design-system",
which npm returns for an unauthorized write. NPM_TOKEN was added on
2026-06-16 and npm write tokens last at most 90 days, so it had likely
expired by the 2026-10-15 publish.

Publishing now authenticates through npm trusted publishing (OIDC): no
NPM_TOKEN or hand-written .npmrc, Node 24, and npm upgraded to 11.5.1+,
which pnpm publish hands the upload to. changesets/action v1 skips its
.npmrc setup when NPM_TOKEN is unset and lets npm use OIDC.

Constraint: trusted publisher on npmjs.com must name release.yml exactly
Rejected: rotate NPM_TOKEN | expires again in 90 days
Rejected: changesets/action v2 | targets Changesets v3, repo is on @changesets/cli 2.x
Confidence: medium
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: actual OIDC publish (needs the npmjs.com trusted publisher setting first)

fix(ThemeProvider): resolve SSR hydration mismatch on syncWithSystem

The initial theme was computed by reading window.matchMedia directly
inside a useState lazy initializer. The server (no window) and the
client's first render (real OS preference) could disagree, producing
a hydration mismatch on every themed element whenever the OS actually
preferred dark.

System-theme detection now goes through useSyncExternalStore, which
keeps the server render and the client's hydration render in
lockstep (both fall back to "light"), then lets React pick up the
real OS value immediately after hydration completes.

opt-in helper for consumers who want to inline a blocking script in
their document <head> and eliminate even that post-hydration flash,
following the same pattern as next-themes.

etc.) that previously got the correct theme from their very first
render with no flash at all — useSyncExternalStore's getServerSnapshot
is only invoked during an actual hydrateRoot pass, never for
createRoot, so this is preserved.
Rejected: plain useEffect-deferred correction (the literal fallback
approach) | always starts every render at "light" regardless of
environment, which would introduce a new flash for pure CSR apps that
never had one.

theme changes while syncWithSystem is on — previously the next OS
change would silently overwrite it. This is an intentional behavior
refinement, confirmed with the package maintainer, not an oversight.
